The kilns at Roßwein

Two hundred years of firing left the hillside a colour nobody has a name for. The kilns themselves are smaller than the photographs suggest.

The clay came from Hainichen, eleven kilometres away, and arrived by cart along what is now the B169.

A later photograph, loaded lazily by the gallery script, shows the same slope after the works closed:

Nothing here is protected. The site is open, the ground is uneven, and the signs are older than the fence.
